Virgil quietly watches over you. If you fall or don\'t respond, Virgil texts and calls your emergency contacts.\n\nLet\'s set things up — just a few simple steps.
The person Virgil will text with your location if you need help.

Virgil watches your phone\'s motion sensor for the shape of a fall: a brief free-fall, a hard impact, then stillness. When all three match, a full-screen 30-second countdown starts. Tap \"I\'m OK\" to cancel. If you don\'t, Virgil texts your emergency contacts your location and calls the primary one.

After setup, turn on \"If I fall\" on the home screen, then drop your phone onto a sofa, a bed, or a thick cushion from at least one metre high (about waist height). The countdown should appear within a few seconds. Never test on a hard surface — you can break the phone and hurt yourself.

At the interval you choose (every few hours during the day), Virgil checks whether you\'ve unlocked or moved the phone recently. If you haven\'t, it rings like a normal call and asks \"Are you there?\". Tap the notification to dismiss it. If you don\'t, a 30-second countdown starts. If you don\'t answer that either, Virgil sends the same alert as a fall — SMS with your location and a call to your primary contact.
If something is happening right now

Press and hold the panic button on the home screen for about a second and a half. Virgil immediately texts your location to every emergency contact and starts a loud siren — no countdown, no call (a screaming siren would make a call useless). The siren is a deterrent against a thief or attacker, not a guarantee: powering off the phone still wins.
Tap the button and unlock your phone with your fingerprint or PIN. Anyone else holding your phone can\'t lower the volume or stop the alarm.
Tap a sound to hear it. Tap again to stop. So you recognise each one when it happens for real.
